statement.p: An open box is to be made out of a 7-inch by 16-inch piece of cardboard by cutting out squares of equal size from the four corners and bending up the sides. If the box needs to be at least 1 inch deep, and no more than 3 inches deep, find the absolute maximum and absolute minimum volumes.

solution.p: You have a rectangle of size 7 by 16, and you cut a square out of each corner. Say each square has length x. Then when you fold the rectangle up, the height of the resulting box is x and the length is 16-2 x while the width is 7 -2 x. So the volume of the box is V=l \cdot w \cdot h = (16 -2 x) (7 -2 x)x= (112-46 x +4 x^2)x=112 x-46 x^2+4x^3 Taking the derivative and setting it equal to 0 gives V'=112-2\cdot 46 x+ 12x^2 =0 Using the quadratic formula, we get that x=\frac{2\cdot46\pm\sqrt{4\cdot46^2-4\cdot 12\cdot 112}}{2\cdot 12}= 1.51793 \mbox{ or } 6.1487406649083 But if x=6.1487406649083, then the width of the box, which is 7-2 x, is negative. So the height is x=1.51793.

Plugging back in, the length of the box is 16-2x=16-2\cdot1.51793=12.9641 and the width is 7-2x=7-2\cdot1.51793=3.96414 And so the volume at the local extremum is 12.9641 \cdot 3.96414 \cdot 1.51793 = 78.0087.
We also calculate the volume at the endpoints, x=1 and x=3. (16-2)(7-2)\cdot 1 = 70, \mbox{ and } (16-6)(7-6)\cdot 3 = 30
So the absolute maximum of volume is 78.0087 and the absolute minimum of volume is 30.
